# Sr Controls Engineer — Disney Experiences (Disneyland Resort)

---
**Job ID:** 10162313
**Date Posted:** Oct 14, 2026
**Date Applied:** Not confirmed. The posting was saved and the tailored resume built on Oct 20, 2026, but there is no Workday confirmation email for it, so Riley is checking whether it was submitted.
**Salary Range:** $130,800–$159,800 per year — Anaheim, CA
---

## Job Summary

A sustaining controls engineering role on the Ride Control side of registered attractions at the Disneyland Resort, reporting to the Sr Manager, Sustaining Engineering. The engineer designs, develops, and troubleshoots PLC hardware and modules with some smaller-scale coding, responds to attraction downtime, leads reliability-improvement projects, analyzes control-system and software hazards, and mentors early-career Cast, with minimal oversight. Full-time, with off-hours and 3rd-shift work as needed.

---

## What You'll Do

- Respond to attraction downtime, supporting Engineering Services' and Operations' urgent needs, including mechanical and control emergencies.
- Scope attraction reliability-improvement efforts through design, install, testing, documentation, and closeout; monitor downtime trends to target them.
- Select systems and equipment that meet design requirements and applicable codes and standards.
- Monitor control-system performance against established criteria; investigate and troubleshoot at the system level and in detail.
- Plan, schedule, and coordinate the technical and management sides of Sustaining Engineering tasks.
- Troubleshoot PLC software and hardware on complex ride systems and understand how ride-system interfaces relate to the attraction's operation.
- Partner with other engineering, maintenance, and operations teams on design and reliability work.
- Perform ride-system hazard analyses, including fault tree analysis and FMEA.
- Ensure compliance with IEEE, NFPA, ASTM, DOSH, NEC/CEC, and similar standards; follow the department change process.
- Stay current on ride-control technology, equipment, and materials.

### Required Qualifications
- Controls systems experience with 5+ years in the amusement park industry or an industrial/manufacturing environment
- Ride element performance analysis: dynamic, kinematic, hydraulic, and pneumatic analysis and calculations
- Electronic control systems and signal processing, including relays and programmable logic controllers
- Electrical motor controls, including variable frequency drives and soft starts
- Industrial automation PLCs such as Rockwell/Allen-Bradley, Siemens, and Mitsubishi
- National and California Electrical Code
- NRTL certifications such as UL, TUV, and ETL
- AutoCAD and ladder logic
- Object-oriented programming (C/C++)
- Wiring and interconnect diagrams
- ANSI, ASTM, and IEEE standards
- Oral and written communication across email, text, and web tools (Slack, SharePoint, Teams)
- Preferred: California Professional Registration; controls circuit design and/or troubleshooting; PDL and ICL; safety PLCs and safety industrial controls; audio/visual systems; systems reliability; scripting in C, VB, JS

### Education
Bachelor of Science from an ABET-accredited engineering program in Electrical Engineering or equivalent with a competitive GPA. Preferred: Master of Science in a technical discipline.

### Benefits
A bonus and/or long-term incentive units may be included, plus the full range of medical, financial, and other benefits depending on level and position. The position is with Walt Disney Parks and Resorts U.S., Inc., part of Disney Experiences.

---

## How I Match Up

### At Application — Oct 20, 2026 (resume built; submission not confirmed)

No submission date is confirmed yet, so this compares the posting against the record as of the day the tailored resume was built.

- **Industrial controls tenure fits:** the record covers designing, wiring, commissioning, and troubleshooting industrial production machines and their control systems in a manufacturing environment since May 2020, which meets the 5+ years industrial/manufacturing path.
- **Controls and electrical overlap:** Allen Bradley PLCs are listed in the skills record; the record also shows Modbus TCP data acquisition (ExtrusionStudio), a multi-board CAN-bus control architecture, servo, linear-motor, and braked NEMA 34 stepper motion, electrical layout and schematics drawn to IEEE conventions, 120/240 VAC machine power, wiring harnesses, and interconnect and panel design. Python, LabVIEW, and JavaScript cover the scripting preference.
- **Reliability and troubleshooting:** cross-functional troubleshooting through after-sales service, control-system performance monitoring in ExtrusionStudio (tolerance-band alarms, out-of-spec timers), and the linear-motor standardization done to simplify service support the reliability and downtime-response duties.
- **Safety work is adjacent:** risk analysis and mitigation to EU and U.S. standards and changes for 2006/42/EC Machinery Directive conformity are on record, but the method (FMEA, fault tree) is not; the [[Career Q&A Log]] has this as an open question.
- **Gaps:** the record does not establish ladder-logic or PLC program authoring (an open Q&A question asks whether PLC work went beyond integration), AutoCAD, C/C++, variable frequency drives or soft starts, NEC/CEC, NRTL certification work, hydraulic or pneumatic analysis, safety PLCs, PDL/ICL, amusement-industry experience, or California Professional Registration. The B.S. in Electro-Mechanical Engineering is close to, but not, the Electrical Engineering degree named.

### Now — Nov 7, 2026

- **Siemens PLCs added to the skills record (Nov 7, 2026):** Riley supports the Siemens PLCs on the filament extrusion lines, which covers a second PLC family the posting names. The ladder-logic, AutoCAD, C/C++, VFD, and code-compliance gaps above are unchanged.
- **Deployment and support facts (Nov 6, 2026):** ExtrusionStudio has been live on all three extrusion lines since October 2026, and Riley is the go-to contact for customer troubleshooting across mechanical faults, electrical faults, and user error, which strengthens the downtime-response and troubleshooting fit.

## About the Company

The role sits in Sustaining Engineering at the Disneyland Resort in Anaheim, providing field engineering support for ride, show, and ride-related control systems. The employer is Walt Disney Parks and Resorts U.S., Inc., part of the business Disney calls Disney Experiences.
